summary:
This week we processed a massive volume of engineering updates, focusing heavily on the evolving intersection of AI agents, supply-chain security, and durable architectural principles. 

**The shift toward agentic workflows** is fundamentally changing how we think about source code and documentation. We’re seeing radical proposals like treating [Markdown in /src](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fhtmx.org%2Fessays%2Fmarkdown-in-src%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0c8d1eb8d-1fa7b778-1561-4656-aaa7-a9f8cabc17a7-000000/6ZBhpn77H5rWTfeU2gg71ZEjhatM-zN7JIxxOWQkU68=452) as an executable artifact and questioning if [frameworks still matter](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fbrookslybrand.com%2Fposts%2Fdo-frameworks-matter-anymore%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0c8d1eb8d-1fa7b778-1561-4656-aaa7-a9f8cabc17a7-000000/_8L729qdLb9pYGpmxgzD-q9GPaMRd61enk6N4z4Tuf8=452) when LLMs can generate boilerplate instantly. There is a growing emphasis on [thinking in systems](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftomtunguz.com%2Fthinking-in-systems%3Futm_source=tldrnewsletter/1/010001a0d82dd699-23eb19a3-47c8-40db-ae2e-ef16d01d6aad-000000/K-c_BTY4R0M27QbAFgbM_XyS7B2udedZb-wJePsq7i8=452) rather than just typing code, alongside warnings that AI-generated code often [lacks the wisdom of long-term maintainability](https://alexn.org/blog/2026/09/22/ai-has-no-wisdom-and-neither-will-you/?utm_source=tldrdevops). To manage this, teams are investing in [robust evaluation systems](https://substack.com/redirect/0d62314e-cce1-4d1c-88da-b898996fa2cb?j=eyJ1IjoiNXJrOXF0In0.DoJwc2vCBtYQD6b7-V0bKy5M_JCBPqObIc6ZNpzy7GY) and addressing the [LLM calibration problem](https://substack.com/redirect/17a9e248-32e7-4240-9d69-ac55dbfd76be?j=eyJ1IjoiNXJrOXF0In0.DoJwc2vCBtYQD6b7-V0bKy5M_JCBPqObIc6ZNpzy7GY) to ensure model confidence matches accuracy.

**Hardening the software supply chain** remains a top priority as researchers uncover how [GitLab email addresses can be weaponized](https://links.tldrnewsletter.com/RmdDFw) and how [AI customer service agents can be hacked](https://www.intigriti.com/researchers/blog/hacking-tools/hacking-ai-customer-service-agents?utm_source=tldrinfosec). Mandiant released a comprehensive blueprint for [securing the SDLC](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/hardening-code-pipelines-and-ci-cd-infrastructure?utm_source=tldrinfosec), while other experts highlighted the [unfinished work in package security](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fnesbitt.io%2F2026%2F09%2F22%2Funfinished-work-in-package-security.html%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0cdfba2d3-f8b0d1bf-8fbc-4759-8a36-218550c40749-000000/GHK0t4B8An8KNgSpomhKmTGk76Wz7uKG-M70l70S2ek=452). On the performance front, Anthropic shared how they made [Claude.ai 3x faster](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fclaude.dev%2Fblog%2Fhow-we-made-claude-ai-faster%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0d31f3ae4-1fe60310-04b6-4338-91dc-ba8745d9ad2a-000000/oLAPmKsYAQL0ND1S5ZZcH0Gs6OOwkzddImeGinZ_hMQ=452) using deterministic benchmarks, while GitHub detailed their migration from CSS-in-JS to [CSS Modules](https://links.tldrnewsletter.com/nw6RTa) to eliminate runtime overhead. We also saw deep dives into distributed systems, including implementing [worker backpressure](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.canva.dev%2Fblog%2Fengineering%2Fworker-backpressure-part-1-how-we-taught-our-queue-workers-to-slow-down%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0cdfba2d3-f8b0d1bf-8fbc-4759-8a36-218550c40749-000000/-fGW18xmOdFks2YoVSOZ9FaDwOfJSPVIY8kvn_i5HB8=452) and how Notion manages [concurrent editing with CRDTs](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.notion.com%2Fblog%2Fhow-notion-handles-concurrent-editing-with-crdts%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0d31f3ae4-1fe60310-04b6-4338-91dc-ba8745d9ad2a-000000/S6NF6YuDSXkttNLjQe-ClYi2BTn1chg8Yr0o8EcTGmY=452).

**New tools for niche workflows** are emerging rapidly, such as [Floci](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Ffloci-io%2Ffloci%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a0cdfba2d3-f8b0d1bf-8fbc-4759-8a36-218550c40749-000000/2tk3KShNwlRPLh9avdsq99kBk6vNQteIvANZPnHYJrI=452) for local AWS emulation and [Ax](https://github.com/google/ax?utm_source=tldrdevops) for orchestrating agent workloads on Kubernetes. For frontend engineers, there are interesting experiments in [detecting element overlap with CSS](https://ishadeed.com/article/css-detect-overlap/?utm_source=tldrdev) and a retrospective on the trade-offs of [migrating between Electron and PWAs](https://kettanaito.com/blog/electron-to-pwa-and-back-again?utm_source=tldrdev).
